2.3a — Health Potions & the Max-Health Cap

You can collect wealth (coins) and suffer damage (spikes). Now you need a way to restore life. Today, you compare the potion to the coin and the spike, discover why healing without a limit creates a game-breaking exploit, and evaluate three different Unity functions for enforcing boundary rules using selection.

Comparative Thinking ~15 min

Notice how our game systems build on each other. When designing the Potion, we ask: what have we already built that works like this?

ComparisonAnalysis
How is the potion similar to the coin? Both are pickups: intangible trigger colliders (Is Trigger = true), handled by OnTriggerEnter2D, and destroyed immediately upon collection so they cannot be grabbed twice.
How is the potion similar to the spike? Both affect health on the StatManager, unlike coins which affect wealth.
How is the potion different from both? It heals (+1 health), but introduces a brand-new constraint: health must never exceed maximum capacity (e.g. 3 hearts). Without a rule, drinking 10 potions gives 13 health!

Enforcing this rule is what the AP CSP framework calls selection: using conditional logic to decide whether or how state changes.

Socratic: Evaluating Multiple Ways to Cap a Value

In Unity C#, there are three common ways to ensure a value does not exceed a maximum limit:

ApproachCode ExampleMechanism
1. Procedural ifif (health > maxHealth) health = maxHealth;Direct selection statement. Simple, easy to read for humans.
2. Mathf.Minhealth = Mathf.Min(health + amount, maxHealth);Mathematical function. Returns the smaller of two numbers.
3. Mathf.Clamphealth = Mathf.Clamp(health + amount, 0, maxHealth);Boundary clamp. Restricts a value between a minimum (0) and maximum.
  1. Why is Mathf.Clamp particularly powerful when managing health? How could a single clamp function handle both dying (falling below 0) and overhealing (rising above maxHealth)?
  2. In what scenarios is an explicit if statement better than Mathf.Min or Mathf.Clamp? (Hint: What if you want to play a special "Buzz / Error" sound only when the player tries to drink at full health?)
  3. Where should this capping logic live — in the Potion script or in StatManager.cs? Why is placing the rule in StatManager better software design?
Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — Create the Potion Prefab.

  1. In the Hierarchy, right-click → 2D Object → Sprite, name it Potion.
  2. Assign a potion sprite from Assets/Artwork.
  3. Add a BoxCollider2D or CircleCollider2D, and check Is Trigger.
  4. At the top of the Inspector, click Tag → Add Tag..., create the tag Potion, and assign it to the Potion.
  5. Drag the Potion GameObject into Assets/Prefabs to make it a reusable prefab!
Read Function-Level Examples ~15 min

Notice how different mathematical capping techniques operate in isolation across completely different systems:

Example 1 — Selection Guard on a Water Reservoir Dam:

// Uses an if statement to enforce an upper ceiling
if (currentGallons > maxReservoirCapacity)
{
    currentGallons = maxReservoirCapacity;
}

Example 2 — Mathematical Ceiling with Mathf.Min on an Electric Scooter Battery:

// Mathf.Min returns the smaller value, preventing the battery from charging past 100%
batteryLevel = Mathf.Min(batteryLevel + chargeAdded, 100f);

Example 3 — Two-Sided Bounding with Mathf.Clamp on a Spaceship Thruster:

// Mathf.Clamp guarantees the output stays between minimum idle (0) and maximum safe power (100)
thrusterPower = Mathf.Clamp(requestedThrust, 0, 100);

Predict Before Building

  1. If currentGallons is 95 and 20 gallons are added, trace Example 1: what is the value before and after the if check?
  2. What is the difference between Mathf.Min (one upper bound) and Mathf.Clamp (both lower and upper bounds)?
  3. Where should health-capping logic live — on the potion GameObject, or inside StatManager? Why is placing the rule in the central manager better software design?
Build Lab: Your Turn ~25 min

Step 1 — Create the Potion Prefab.

  1. In the Hierarchy, right-click → 2D Object → Sprite, name it Potion.
  2. Assign a potion sprite from Assets/Artwork.
  3. Add a BoxCollider2D or CircleCollider2D, and check Is Trigger.
  4. At the top of the Inspector, click Tag → Add Tag..., create the tag Potion, and assign it to the Potion.
  5. Drag the Potion GameObject into Assets/Prefabs to make it a reusable prefab!
Architectural Specification for StatManager.cs:

Enforce the Max Health Ceiling:

  • What variable represents the maximum health a player can hold? How do you expose it as a tuning knob in the Inspector?
  • Where should the rule live that prevents health from exceeding maximum capacity? Should it be on every potion, or centralized inside StatManager?
  • Inside your health modification method, after adjusting health, how can you guarantee the value never exceeds maximum capacity?
  • What conditional check or mathematical bounding function (such as Mathf.Min or Mathf.Clamp) can you use to enforce this ceiling?
Architectural Specification for PlayerController.cs:

Handle Potion Trigger:

  • What function does this belong in?
  • Should this be a trigger or a collider?
  • How do you check if the object is a Potion?
  • How do you check to see if the StatManager exists before communicating with it?
  • What function on the manager do you call to change health?
  • Should you be able to go above maxHealth? How would you prevent this from happening, and what do you need to check?
  • How do you destroy the potion? Is the potion other.gameObject or is it gameObject? (Hint: this script is attached to gameObject; we collided with other).

Save both files and press Play! Walk into spikes to drop your health to 2, then walk into a potion: your health restores to 3. Walk into another potion while at full health: your health stays capped at 3 instead of climbing to 4!

Bug Hunt: Testing Boundary Conditions

  1. What happens if you change maxHealth to 5 in the Inspector? Does the code still cap correctly, or did you hardcode the number 3 anywhere?
  2. What happens if you accidentally write health < maxHealth in the capping check? Trace what happens when health is 2.
  3. What happens if you forget to check Is Trigger on the Potion prefab? Does OnTriggerEnter2D run?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Testing Mathf.Clamp

  1. In StatManager.cs, try rewriting your ceiling check using Mathf.Clamp to bound health between 0 (death) and maxHealth in a single line. Test taking damage on spikes and healing with potions. Does this one function replace multiple if statements?
  2. Game Design Question: Should a player at full health be allowed to consume a potion and waste it, or should the potion stay on the ground until needed? How would you implement that check in PlayerController.cs?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain how potions are similar to coins, similar to spikes, and different from both
  • Define selection and explain how it prevents the overheal exploit
  • Compare three ways to bound values in C# (if, Mathf.Min, Mathf.Clamp)
  • Create a new prefab with appropriate collider settings and custom tags
  • Commit your working potion healing system to GitHub
